key_insight: Unsupervised autoencoders trained only for reconstruction can still learn latent spaces that align with physically meaningful aerodynamic variables and laws.
engineering_relevance: This suggests reduced-order models and flow surrogates can discover interpretable flow parameters without explicit physics labels, which is useful for design, control, and uncertainty-aware analysis.
method: Train autoencoders on aerodynamic databases of increasing complexity, from linear theory to nonlinear separated RANS flows.
Use sequential training to decouple inviscid flow structure from boundary-layer effects in a 3D latent space.
Assess whether latent coordinates align with physical variables via cross-validated regression and affine-alignment metrics.
evidence_signal: Across independent trainings, the latent organization is reproducible and quantitatively linked to physical parameters; one latent variable strongly correlates with Reynolds number and aerodynamic drag.
watch_item: Latent coordinates are not uniquely identifiable under random initialization, so interpretation requires post-hoc alignment and careful validation before using them as direct physical variables.
paper_title: Physically Organized Latent Spaces in Unsupervised Autoencoders: Evidence from Aerodynamic Databases
